product.name: PAINT RUSH - executive demo of on-site paint mixing cost
product.description: An 8-bit, Game Boy-style browser demo showing that while staff mix tins to order, the shop floor is empty and walk-ins leave without buying; then the same day replayed with large orders sent to a central hub.
product.note: The backlog when tracker.kind is local or none. Plan: docs/plan-paint-rush.md. Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md.

scaffold.title: Project scaffold with a Game Boy canvas and an offline single-file build
scaffold.description: Set up the project so every later ticket has gates, a screen and a build. Vite + TypeScript, run with Bun. A 160x144 canvas scaled by whole-pixel factors and centred (letterboxed), drawn only in the four Game Boy greens defined once in src/styles/tokens.css. A placeholder title screen reading PAINT RUSH and PRESS SPACE. `bun run build` emits one self-contained HTML file (all JS, CSS and assets inlined) that runs from file:// with no network, for presenting from a laptop.
acceptance_criteria: package.json has dev, build, test, typecheck, lint and check scripts; `bun run check` runs typecheck, lint and tests and passes
src/styles/tokens.css defines the four palette colours; no other file under src/ holds a raw colour literal (check ui passes)
The canvas keeps a 160x144 logical resolution, scales by an integer factor, uses nearest-neighbour rendering, and stays fully visible at phone and desktop viewports
`bun run build` produces dist/paint-rush.html; opening it via file:// with networking disabled shows the title screen (a Playwright test asserts this)
.forger/ui.json paths, tokens, start and url match the real project, and `screenshot` writes docs/screenshots/index-*.png
Playwright and axe-core are dev dependencies; `check a11y` passes on the title screen
README.md says what the demo is and how to run, build and present it
reuse: vite-plugin-singlefile (or equivalent) for the inlined build
docs/design/two-run-results wireframe for the title screen content

sim-engine.title: Deterministic shop simulation for the today and hub scenarios
sim-engine.description: The model behind the demo, pure and tested, with no rendering. An event-driven simulation in shop minutes over one shift, driven by a seeded RNG and a parameter object (defaults in GLOSSARY.md and docs/plan-paint-rush.md). Walk-ins arrive at a Poisson rate; a free staff member serves them for the service time and they spend the average sale; otherwise they wait and leave as a lost sale at the patience limit. Mix orders arrive at their own rate with a tin count from the order-size mix and tin sizes priced per size; a free staff member takes the order and is off the floor for minutes-per-tin x tins. Scenario `today` mixes everything in store; scenario `hub` sends large orders (over the hub threshold) to the central hub, which records a 2h delivery and never occupies staff. Both scenarios share one seed so arrivals are identical (ADR 0001). Output: per-scenario metrics and an ordered event timeline the renderer can replay.
acceptance_criteria: Same seed and parameters give an identical timeline and metrics; different seeds differ
The today and hub runs for one seed have identical walk-in and mix-order arrival times and tin counts
In hub, no order above the hub threshold is mixed in store; each appears as a hub dispatch with a delivery time 120 shop minutes later
A walk-in who waits past the patience limit is recorded as a lost sale worth the average sale; one served in time is not
With one staff member mixing, a walk-in arriving during the mix finds nobody free (floor empty)
Metrics include tins mixed in store, orders sent to hub, walk-ins served, walk-ins lost, sales lost GBP and staff minutes off the floor
`bun run sim --json [--seed n]` prints both scenarios' metrics as JSON; a test runs it
Engine code imports nothing from the DOM or the renderer
reuse: GLOSSARY.md terms for type and field names

shop-scene.title: Animated shop scene that replays one scenario
shop-scene.description: Waits for the owner to approve the wireframe at docs/design/shop-scene/ (set status to not_started to release). Replays one scenario's timeline on the Game Boy canvas at the time scale (default 1 real second = 5 shop minutes, ADR 0002) with original pixel art only: a top-down shop floor with door, aisles and counter; a mixing room behind a wall; staff walking between them; walk-ins queueing with a wait meter, an '!' bubble and walking out with a '-GBP95' pop; a tin progress bar ('TIN 3/8'); a status bar with scenario name, shop clock, served and lost counters and GBP lost; a Pokemon-style text box with narration beats. In hub, a van leaves the loading bay with '2H DELIVERY' for each large order.
acceptance_criteria: The rendered counters at the end of a replay equal the sim-engine metrics for the same seed
Replay length equals shift length / time scale (8h at 1 s = 5 min plays in 96 s), within one frame
The floor is drawn empty whenever the timeline says no staff member is on it
All sprites and tiles are original and drawn in the four token colours; no third-party game assets
The UI states in the wireframe (opening, overflow queue, no-canvas fallback) are implemented
docs/screenshots/ is updated by `screenshot`, and docs/design/shop-scene/ is moved into docs/progress/ per the archive rule

two-run-results.title: Presentation flow: today, results, with hub, comparison
two-run-results.description: Waits for the owner to approve the wireframe at docs/design/two-run-results/. The full pitch on SPACE: title -> today replay -> today results -> hub replay (same seed) -> comparison. Comparison shows today vs hub for walk-ins lost and sales lost, then sales saved per day, per week, per year and across N stores, with the footnote 'Excludes central prep and delivery costs.' R reshuffles the day (new seed) and replays. Results are mirrored into a visually hidden live region.
acceptance_criteria: SPACE advances through every step in order; at the comparison it replays the same day, R starts a new seed
Comparison figures equal the sim-engine metrics; week, year and store extrapolations use the parameters for trading days and stores
The excludes-costs footnote is always shown on the comparison
Large GBP values are shortened to fit the text box (e.g. GBP1.2M) and a zero-loss day reads 'No sales lost today'
The live region contains the comparison as text, and `check a11y` passes on every step
docs/screenshots/ is updated and docs/design/two-run-results/ is moved into docs/progress/ per the archive rule

settings.title: Settings menu to edit every demo parameter
settings.description: Waits for the owner to approve the wireframe at docs/design/settings/. A Game Boy-style menu opened with S from the title, by keyboard or touch: shift hours, time scale, staff on floor (1-4), walk-ins per hour, mix orders per hour, service time, patience, average sale, minutes per tin, order-size mix, tin prices per size, hub threshold, stores, trading days per year. Reshuffle and reset-to-defaults actions. Values persist in browser storage and feed the next run.
acceptance_criteria: Every parameter in src/sim/params.ts is editable from the menu and the next run uses the edited value
Order-size percentages that do not total 100 show 'MUST TOTAL 100' and block BACK
Values survive a reload; with storage unavailable they still apply for the session and a note says so
Reset restores the documented defaults
The menu is fully operable by keyboard and by touch (tap a row to select it, on-screen -/+ to change a value) and `check a11y` passes
docs/screenshots/ is updated and docs/design/settings/ is moved into docs/progress/ per the archive rule

take-control.title: Take-control mode for the presenter
take-control.description: An optional mode, toggled with C during a replay, where the presenter decides what a free staff member does next when a walk-in and a mix order are both waiting. Autoplay stays the default. The simulation must expose a decision hook so the same engine serves both modes deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: With no input the mode behaves exactly like autoplay
A choice changes the outcome and the metrics reflect it
The engine accepts a decision policy; autoplay is the default policy and is covered by the existing tests
The on-screen prompt says which keys choose what
reuse: shop-scene text box for the prompt

chiptune-sound.title: Chiptune sound effects, muted by default
chiptune-sound.description: Original square-wave effects generated with the Web Audio API for walk-in, walkout, tin done and van leaving. Muted on load; M toggles and the status bar shows the state. A finger-sized on-screen sound button (beside RESHUFFLE, same style, 44x44 minimum) toggles it on touch devices. No audio files.
acceptance_criteria: No sound plays until M is pressed or the sound button is tapped
The sound button is keyboard focusable, at least 44x44 CSS px, and its label says whether sound is on
Each named event triggers its effect when unmuted
No audio file is added; effects are synthesised
The built single file still runs offline

tap-input.title: Touch input so the demo works on phones and tablets
tap-input.description: Owner report: on mobile the demo cannot be advanced because there is no SPACE key. Every keyboard action must also work by touch. A tap or click anywhere on the game screen does what SPACE does (start, skip narration, advance, replay). Actions bound to other keys get a touch equivalent: reshuffle (R) and sound (M) as small on-screen buttons in the letterbox area or under the screen, sized for a finger, styled in the palette. On touch devices the prompts read TAP instead of PRESS SPACE. Keyboard behaviour is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A tap on the canvas advances every step of the flow exactly as SPACE does (Playwright test with touch emulation at the phone viewport)
Reshuffle and sound toggle are reachable by touch, at least 44x44 CSS px, and keyboard focusable
On a touch device the title and results prompts say TAP; on desktop they still say PRESS SPACE
Taps do not zoom or scroll the page (touch-action and viewport set) and a double tap does not skip two steps by accident
Keyboard controls are unchanged and their tests still pass
docs/screenshots/ updated; the previous set is first copied into docs/progress/ per the archive rule
reuse: the existing SPACE handler: route taps through the same input action rather than a parallel path

v2-style-frame.title: v2 style frame: a playful 8-bit shop the audience recognises
v2-style-frame.description: The look for v2, built and shown before anything plays on it (docs/plan-paint-rush-v2.md, ADR 0003). Replace the four-green palette with a limited 8-bit handheld palette with real colour, all in src/styles/tokens.css. Draw the screen inside a handheld console frame (shell, screen bezel, power LED, A/B-style action buttons as placeholders). Redraw the shop at a scale where each thing reads at a glance on a projector and a phone: a checkered floor, the tinting machine and shaker in the back, the till on a counter, a colour-swatch wall, shelves of tins, plants; a shop assistant and at least four visibly different customers with drop shadows; a speech bubble with an order ('10 TINS'); colour-coded patience bars; a red COUNTER UNMANNED banner. Expose it as ?scene=style-frame (a fixed composed moment: a 10-tin order at the till, a queue of three, one customer about to walk out) and keep presenter mode working on the new art. This ticket is the owner's approval gate for v2.
acceptance_criteria: ?scene=style-frame renders the composed moment described above in the console frame, at phone and desktop sizes
Every colour comes from tokens in src/styles/tokens.css; the palette-only tests are replaced by a test that every drawn colour is a defined token
Each listed prop and character is drawn as original pixel art, with no asset, font or likeness from an existing game
Presenter mode (the v1 flow) still plays end to end on the new art and its tests pass
A short capture (video or GIF) of presenter mode on the new art and the style-frame screenshots are linked from the PR, with a paragraph on how the look serves the brief quoted in the v2 plan
The v1 screenshots are archived into docs/progress/ before being overwritten
reuse: the existing scene and replay code; change the art, not the model

v2-play-mode.title: v2 play mode: two short rounds where you are the shop assistant
v2-play-mode.description: Style frame approved by the owner. The default experience. Round 1 (TODAY): every mix order is mixed in store. Round 2 (WITH HUB): orders over the hub threshold can be sent to the hub with one press. Each round is short (default 40 s, editable) and plays a busy slice of the day at a faster round time scale. The opening is scripted: a 10-tin trade order is at the till at second 0 and a queue starts forming. The player chooses every action with big labelled console buttons: SERVE (for the customer at the till), MIX N TINS (locks the till for N tins), SEND TO HUB (round 2, large orders only). Keys, clicks and taps all work. The simulation stays the model: arrivals come from the sim with the round seed, the same in both rounds, and the player's choices are the decision policy (src/sim/control.ts). Each round ends on a short result: captured, walked out, time unmanned, sent to hub.
acceptance_criteria: Both rounds face identical arrivals for one seed, and the scripted 10-tin order is at the till at second 0 of each
MIX N TINS takes the assistant off the floor for N tins at the round time scale; the COUNTER UNMANNED banner shows exactly while nobody is on the floor
SEND TO HUB is offered only in round 2 and only for orders over the hub threshold, and keeps the assistant at the till
Every action works by key, click and tap; buttons show what they will do and are disabled with a reason when not available
Round results come from the sim's metrics for the choices made (unit tests drive the policy with scripted choices)
A Playwright test plays both rounds on a phone viewport with touch
A capture of a played round is linked from the PR
On a phone the console frame shrinks (or drops decoration) so the game screen takes most of the width, while the SERVE / MIX / HUB buttons stay finger-sized

v2-debrief.title: v2 debrief: from two played rounds to a whole real day
v2-debrief.description: Style frame approved by the owner. Ties the felt problem to the evidence. Title offers PLAY (default) and PRESENTER. After round 2, a round comparison, then 'NOW A WHOLE REAL DAY': the existing full-shift today vs hub replay at the full-shift time scale, then the comparison with per day, week, year and estate figures and the excludes-costs footnote. The full-shift debrief always uses autoplay, so its comparison stays like-for-like (ADR 0001).
acceptance_criteria: PLAY runs round 1 -> round 1 result -> round 2 -> round comparison -> whole-day replays -> estate comparison
PRESENTER runs the v1 flow unchanged on the new art
The whole-day comparison equals the sim metrics for autoplay, whatever the player chose in the rounds
Every step advances by key, click and tap; the live region carries each result as text
Screenshots of every step updated, previous set archived

v2-customer-types.title: v2 customer types: show which sales walk out
v2-customer-types.description: Style frame approved by the owner. Walk-ins become types with their own value, look and bubble: colour advice, sample pot, small purchase, alongside mix orders. Default values and shares average to the configured average sale (GBP95), so the headline numbers do not move unless the owner edits them. Types and values are editable in settings; the round and whole-day results show lost sales by type.
acceptance_criteria: With default settings the mean walk-in value equals the average sale parameter (unit test over many seeds)
Each type has a distinct bubble and sprite variation
Results list lost sales by type
Settings edit type shares and values, with shares validated to total 100

v2-juice.title: v2 juice: every action gets feedback
v2-juice.description: Style frame approved by the owner. Each player action and game event answers with motion, sound and a visual change: buttons press down; the dialogue arrow bounces; the shaker jitters with a low hum while mixing; a till chime and a +GBP floater on a sale; a descending coin jingle, a red flash and a -GBP floater on a walkout; a van whoosh on SEND TO HUB; the patience bar shakes when nearly empty. Sound stays muted by default with a visible SFX button on the console; motion respects reduced-motion.
acceptance_criteria: A table in the code maps every action and event to its visual, motion and sound, and a test asserts every event in the timeline has an entry
With reduced motion, jitter, shake and flash are off and the information still shows
No audio file is added; effects are synthesised; nothing plays until sound is enabled
A capture of a round with sound on is linked from the PR
The SFX toggle lives on the console frame, not floating outside it, and stays keyboard focusable and 44x44 CSS px

v2-capture.title: v2 capture: a recorded play-through for the slide deck
v2-capture.description: Style frame approved by the owner. A command that plays a scripted round and the debrief headlessly and writes a video and a GIF to docs/screenshots/, so the owner can drop the demo into slides if the room has no browser.
acceptance_criteria: `bun run capture` writes docs/screenshots/play-through.webm and .gif from a fixed seed and scripted choices
The previous capture is archived into docs/progress/ first
README says how to regenerate it
reuse: the e2e play test's scripted choices
